## 1601 N Milwaukee Ave — Zoning & Development Assessment
**PIN:** 14313320180000 | West Town (Community Area 24)

---

### 1. Zoning District

This parcel is zoned **B3-2 (Community Shopping District)**, established by ordinance #17230 dated May 4, 2011, with the map record last updated December 15, 2021. This has not been recently rezoned. Verify at the [Chicago Zoning Map](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning).

---

### 2. Ground-Floor Retail + Apartments Above

**Yes, this is a permitted-by-right use.** [1] expressly states that B3 accommodates a broad range of retail and service uses, and [2] confirms that dwelling units located above the ground floor are permitted by right (P) in B3 districts. Ground-floor retail paired with residential above is the paradigmatic B3 mixed-use form.

---

### 3. Bulk & Density Standards

From the zoning table for B3-2 (§17-3-0104 [1]):

| Standard | Value |
|---|---|
| **FAR** | 2.2 |
| **Max Height** | 45–50 ft (varies by lot frontage & ground-floor commercial) |
| **Min Lot Area per Dwelling Unit** | 1,000 sq ft |
| **Max Units (lot-area basis only)** | ~11 units (11,951 sq ft ÷ 1,000 = 11) |
| **Lot Coverage / Setbacks** | Not specified in the retrieved code text |

The 11-unit figure is a **lot-area ceiling only** — FAR, height, parking, and other standards may allow fewer units; efficiency/SRO units may allow more [3]. Setbacks were not in the retrieved code text; confirm at the Department of Buildings or in §17-3-0400 [3] directly.

---

### 4. Overlays & Special Designations

This parcel carries **multiple significant overlays**:

- **Milwaukee Avenue District (HD-56) — Chicago Landmark Historic District:** Any permit to alter, demolish, add to, or construct a new structure within this district requires the **Commission on Chicago Landmarks' written approval** (§2-120-740). This is a binding constraint on all physical changes.

- **Noel State Bank — Individual Chicago Landmark:** The existing building is individually landmarked. A permit to alter, demolish, or add to it also requires Commission on Chicago Landmarks' written approval (§2-120-740). The building carries a **CHRS "orange" rating** in the Chicago Historic Resources Survey under the name "Noel State Bank."

- **Wicker Park Historic District — National Register of Historic Places:** Federal listing. Does not impose local permit review but may affect eligibility for federal Historic Tax Credits if rehabilitating.

- **Transit-Oriented Development (CTA):** The parcel is within the CTA transit-served area (Damen Blue Line station is 0.07 miles away). [4] and [5] govern transit-served location standards. See item 5 below.

- **ADU-Allowed Area — Zone 8:** Coach houses and conversion units are permitted by right under §17-3-0207. Annual limits, owner-occupancy limits, and administrative adjustment requirements apply (§17-7-0573, §17-7-0574).

- **Affordable Requirements Ordinance (ARO) Zone:** Any residential development triggering an ARO entitlement must comply with affordable unit requirements. The West Town community area has 20 ARO projects totaling 291 affordable units already in the pipeline.

- **Wicker Park Special Service Area (SSA):** A special service area levy applies; the tax breakdown confirms a City of Chicago Special Service Area 33 levy of approximately $2,363/year on this parcel.

No Planned Development or Lakefront Protection overlay applies here.

---

### 5. Parking & Transit Reduction

B3-2 is a transit-served location under §17-10-0102-B [5]. Because the Damen Blue Line station is 0.07 miles away (well within the 2,640-foot threshold), the **minimum parking requirement may be reduced by up to 100%** — meaning zero off-street parking spaces are required by right. No density, FAR, or height bonus applies at the B3-**2** dash level; those bonuses are available only in dash-3 districts [3].

---

### 6. Demolition & New Construction — What Approvals Apply?

A demolition-and-rebuild scenario here faces **serious constraints**:

- **Individual Landmark (Noel State Bank):** The Commission on Chicago Landmarks must approve demolition in writing before any permit can issue (§2-120-740). Demolition of an individually designated Chicago Landmark is extraordinarily difficult to obtain; the Commission considers economic hardship, architectural significance, and alternatives.

- **Milwaukee Avenue Landmark Historic District (HD-56):** Even if the individual landmark status were somehow resolved, new construction within the district also requires Commission approval for design compatibility.

- **Transit-Served Location Standards:** New construction within 2,640 feet of a CTA rail station must satisfy §17-3-0308 [4], including compliance with parking standards (§17-10-0102-B) and pedestrian-street standards (§17-3-0504).

- **Milwaukee Ave Traffic:** The measured segment between W North Ave and N Wood St carries about 11,342 vehicles/day — a high-activity corridor.

- **If demolition were approved**, a new mixed-use building could be built by right at up to 2.2 FAR, 45–50 ft height, ~11 residential units (lot-area basis), zero parking required, with ARO affordable-unit obligations if triggered. ADUs would also be permitted by right (§17-3-0207).

**Bottom line:** Rehabilitation or adaptive reuse is far more feasible than demolition here. Any path forward — demolition or significant exterior alteration — requires a pre-application meeting with the Commission on Chicago Landmarks before a building permit can be filed.

---

### Confidence & What Could Not Be Determined

- **High confidence:** Zoning district, FAR, height range, per-unit lot area, overlay designations, parking reduction, landmark status.
- **Moderate confidence:** Setbacks and lot coverage are not in the retrieved code text; confirm in §17-3-0400 [3].
- **Not determined:** Assessed value (no assessment history in county records for this PIN); sale history (none on record).
- **Code vintage:** Municipal Code text current through the Council Journal of March 18, 2026. A later amendment may not be reflected.

**How to verify:** Zoning — [Chicago Zoning Map](https://gisapps.chicago.gov/ZoningMapWeb/?liab=1&config=zoning). Landmark status — Commission on Chicago Landmarks (312-744-3200). Permits and violations — Chicago Buildings portal (chicago.gov/buildings). ARO obligations — DHED (312-744-5000).
